title: Bounded heads during loop startup
statement: Let $body$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $anchor$ be a state of $body$, let $x$ and $s$ be Boolean words, let $t$ and $B$ be natural numbers, and let $fuel$ be a configuration of $F$ on input $x$. Suppose that the run of $body$ from its initial configuration on $x$ is never in state $anchor$ at any time $u<t$, that at time $t$ it is exactly the seam configuration with state $anchor$ and word $s$, that its space use is at most $B$ at every time $u\le t$, and that every work-tape head of $fuel$ lies between $-B$ and $B$. Then, for the loop-host machine in non-search mode started in its ready configuration with fuel $fuel$, every work-tape head lies between $-(B+2)$ and $B+2$ at each time $u\le t+2$.

fuel is an F configuration on input x
